claims.text: Existing predictive methods for HfNbTaTiZr assume perfect, defect-free bulk crystals.
The proposed predictive approach incorporates atomic-scale defects and defect interactions.
Including atomic-scale defects and interactions will improve the accuracy of predicted thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is defect-free.
Atomic-scale defects scatter phonons in HfNbTaTiZr.
Previous models do not account for defect scattering of phonons.
The proposed model will predict thermal-conductivity values that differ significantly from defect-free estimates.
Defects have a larger effect on thermal conductivity at lower temperatures.
The model is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
The model is applicable across varying defect concentrations.
The magnitude of the model's accuracy improvement depends on defect type and concentration.
Comparisons at 200 K, 600 K, and 1200 K between samples with controlled defect concentrations and both models can test the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial material is declared defect-free, but defects are simultaneously treated as present within the alloy and varied experimentally; no physical intervention for introducing controlled defects is specified.
The mechanism concerns phonon transport, but the predicted outcome and measurements refer only to undifferentiated thermal conductivity, without separating lattice and electronic contributions.
